connect.description: Organon automatically queries about twenty taxonomic databases (GBIF, ITIS, AlgaeBase, WoRMS…) to generate a sourced draft of a Wikipedia article on a taxon.
connect.restricted: Generation is restricted to signed-in Wikimedia accounts. It will later be possible to publish or update an article directly from this tool.

storage.banner: This site can remember your preferences (day/night theme, and future search features) in your browser's local storage, for 365 days at most. No data is sent to a third party or to Organon.

search.placeholder: scientific name, vernacular name or QID…
search.input_label: Scientific name, vernacular name or Wikidata QID
search.help_text: Enter a scientific name, a vernacular name or a Wikidata QID. Suggestions appear as you type; a list of candidates is only offered if the name is ambiguous (homonyms, vernacular name with several results). The filter narrows the suggestions and resolves homonyms across domains.
search.candidates_title: Several taxa match “{query}” — choose the one to open:

authors.title: Authors and credits
authors.organon_intro: It is a tool somewhere between a rewrite of Taxobot in Python – a sort of heir – and a little bird that has taken flight to explore new horizons.
authors.organon_developer_after: is the developer of this website.
authors.taxobot_after: , to generate article skeletons for taxa from third-party taxonomic databases (GBIF, ITIS, WoRMS, Catalogue of Life, EOL, NCBI, etc.).
authors.wikipedia_before: The Wikipedia community, and in particular the members of the Biology project, was the driving force behind its creation. Let's discuss it over a
authors.wikipedia_after: and, above all, feel free to contribute to making biology more accessible on Wikipedia (or elsewhere).
